card.title: Playstation 4 Fault finding with UART

claims.statement: PS4 UART output is blank unless the UART flag is enabled in the NOR: dump the NOR (WSON8 on CUH-12xx/Slim/Pro, 16-pin SOP on CUH-10xx/11xx) at least twice, verify matching dumps in PS4 Wee Tools, set the UART flag and write it back; keep the original dump safe as it holds per-console data.
'DCT[x/y] is disabled' means a RAM block (pairs 0/1, 2/3, 4/5, 6/7) failed—RAM or the APU connection.

'loadBios -8' / 'sceSblSlLoadSelf -8' means syscon isn't decrypting CoreOS: faulty RAM (enable the memory test flag; replace all RAM if it fails) or corrupted CoreOS (swap the CoreOS slot with a syscon flasher).
Looping SAMU enter/leave points at the APU; 'EAP key not available' can be recovered in Wee Tools; IDPS error has no fix; last line 'timer_mtk0 ... on pci0' indicates a failed crystal oscillator.

procedure: Dump NOR twice (in-circuit with 3.3 V external supply or removed); compare in Wee Tools.
Validate the NOR; enable the UART flag; write it.
Solder TX/RX/GND per board revision; use a 3.3 V USB-TTL.
Open Wee Tools terminal and power on.
Match the last/error line to the fault list.
cautions: SOURCE RISK: Losing the original NOR dump permanently bricks the console—verify dumps first.
card.caveats: Community-written Repair Wiki page, paraphrased; check the linked page (and its images) before acting on a reading.
